description: AstroTech is a team of six engineering students from the University of Jordan, passionate about space, technology, and innovation. We combine our diverse engineering skills to develop creative, data-driven solutions to real-world challenges and explore new possibilities through NASA Space Apps.
summary: LunaScope is an interactive 3D lunar mission simulator and trajectory analysis platform designed to solve the critical operational risks of exploring the Moon’s south pole.   Lunar south-pole missions face extreme constraints: steep crater walls cast long shadows that cut solar power generation, while rugged terrain and Earthset interrupt Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communications. Static mission plans fail when launch delays shift these narrow visibility windows.   Powered by an authentic Python science engine integrating NASA open data—including DE421 ephemeris, LOLA topography, LROC WAC imagery, and CLPS vehicle catalogs—LunaScope calculates real-time SPICE geometry and 5-kilometer terrain ray-casting. Through an intuitive web interface, mission engineers and students can simulate launches, pilot rovers across lunar ridges, manage battery budgets, and dynamically evaluate how launch delays impact solar exposure and Earth visibility. By transforming complex orbital physics into actionable insight, LunaScope helps reduce mission failure risks and makes lunar exploration accessible to everyone.
details:
1. What does it do & How does it work?

LunaScope is an interactive 3D lunar mission simulator and trajectory analysis platform designed for the Moon’s south pole. It simulates extreme operational constraints, allowing mission engineers and students to launch, steer across lunar terrain, manage battery power under harsh solar lighting, and evaluate Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication links. The system computes real-time SPICE geometry and 5-kilometer terrain ray-casting to evaluate shadowing and visibility windows.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

Lunar south-pole missions face a high historical failure risk and severe launch delay costs due to complex lighting conditions. LunaScope transforms complex orbital physics into actionable insight, helping mission planners optimize launch windows, track communication dropouts, and ensure rover survival. For education, it provides an intuitive platform to visualize celestial mechanics.

3. Tools, Software & Technologies Used

  • Backend & Science Engine: Python, JavaScript, and specialized ephemeris/topography pipelines.
  • Data Sources: NASA open datasets including DE421 ephemeris, LOLA topography, LROC WAC imagery, and CLPS vehicle catalogs.
  • Testing & Reliability: Automated integration test suites and modular architecture separating scientific calculations from the UI.

4. Creativity & Team Considerations

LunaScope stands out by bridging high-precision NASA scientific data with real-time interactive simulation, replacing static reports with dynamic operational control. The team prioritized a lightweight, modular architecture capable of scaling to multi-site lunar exploration and future orbital relay integrations.
